# 1 Clement Chapter 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_006_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 6

**6:1** To these men who conducted their lives in a holy manner there was gathered together a great multitude of the chosen, who through many indignities and tortures — being the victims of jealousy — set among us a most fair example.

**6:2** Because of jealousy women were persecuted, being Danaids and Dirces, and after suffering dreadful and unholy torments, they ran with surety the course of faith and received a noble prize, despite being weak in body.

**6:3** Jealousy has estranged wives from their husbands, and destroyed the saying of our father Adam: "This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh." [Gen 2:23]

**6:4** Jealousy and strife have overthrown great cities and uprooted mighty nations.

---

*EMET: "Danaids and Dirces" — possibly a reference to theatrical-style executions where Christian women were costumed as mythological figures condemned to punishment. Danaid: condemned to pour water into a perforated vessel forever. Dirce: tied to a bull. Both were modes of execution used in the Neronian persecution.*
